newsitem.title: FRANCE: Framatome merger talks fail on GEC stake.
newsitem.headline: Framatome merger talks fail on GEC stake.

text.p: French state-controlled nuclear engineering group Framatome said on Monday a planned merger with GEC-Alsthom seemed unlikely to be achieved.

It said that Britain's General Electric Company Plc had sought a stake of 50 percent in the group that would have been created, equal to its current stake in the GEC Alsthom joint-venture with Alcatel Alsthom .
But this wish went against a government-imposed condition that French interests keep a majority in the nuclear group.
Framatome also said its 1996 net profit rose to 894 million francs, from 663 million last year, on lower sales of 15.2 billion francs in 1996 against 17.9 billion francs last year.
Its order book rose to 32.8 billion francs from 27.4 billion francs.
In a statement, Framatome said its supervisory board had met on April 4 and had underlined the strategic interest of an alliance in the medium and long term both for Framatome and GEC Alsthom.

It said that the main shareholders of Framatome had told the board that "the completion of the merger in line with the original conditions was unlikely and that they continued to explore the conditions in which the sought-after industrial synergies can be obtained in a manner acceptable to all".
Framatome is 44 percent owned by Alcatel Alsthom. The rest is held by state-owned groups CEA Industrie, Electricite de France (EDF) and the Consortium de Realisation (CDR).

Alcatel chairman Serge Tchuruk said on March 18 the talks about a merger between Framatome and GEC Alsthom had run into difficulties and he added that Alcatel and GEC were now in talks about wider cooperation than the GEC Alsthom venture for industrial power and high speed trains.

Industry Minister Franck Borotra last year imposed five conditions on a Framatome merger. They included France keeping control over its nuclear destiny and Framatome continuing work with Siemens AG on a new nuclear reactor.

Borotra on Friday invited GEC to start talks with either Alcatel or Lagardere Group about joining a bid for the state's 58 percent stake in defence electronics group Thomson-CSF after the government said it could not accept a stand-alone GEC bid for Thomson-CSF on grounds of national security.
